inputs.text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has granted regular bail to a man booked under national-security provisions and the Official Secrets Act over alleged telephone contact with Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri.” Bail is not acquittal, but when Pakistan and sensitive information are involved, the public deserves more than a case that falters for lack of solid evidence. The authorities have a duty to protect the country—and to do the painstaking work needed to prove their case. If they rely on suspicion instead, they risk letting a genuine security threat walk free while weakening public trust in the institutions meant to keep us safe.
